templates.why_chosen: The corpus's clearest flow-type legend: a 'Legends' block naming inter-device data (black solid), intra-device data (blue solid) and control (orange dashed).
templates.what_to_learn: Name every arrow class explicitly in an in-figure legend; three classes is the practical maximum and dashed should be reserved for control.

templates.why_chosen: Star-rated, high-rank figure the reference doc itself cites as the canonical times-N annotation: 16 identical PIM Ctrl/GDDR6-PIM channels are drawn once, marked '×16', with an inside legend naming inter-device, intra-device, and control flow.
templates.what_to_learn: For a very large, fixed replica count, skip the ellipsis and just draw one instance with a bold '×16' label beside it; keep the flow-type legend (inter-device solid black, intra-device solid blue, control dashed orange) inside the frame since it is what makes the single-device diagram legible.

templates.why_chosen: A PIM/CXL device floorplan: 16 identical PIM Ctrl/GDDR6-PIM compute-memory pairs sit in a row (the ×N rule this section borrows from replicated-grid) with an inside legend naming three traffic classes crossing the chip.
templates.what_to_learn: When one chip repeats the same compute-plus-memory pair many times, draw it once with a ×N label rather than a full grid, and legend the traffic classes crossing the chip (inter-device, intra-device, control) so the reader can tell a peer-to-peer hop from a local one.
